23 24 --- 25 26 ## Table of Contents 27 28 - [Overview](#overview) 29 - [Features](#features) 30 - [Quick Start](#quick-start) 31 - [Architecture](#architecture) 32 - [Configuration](#configuration) 33 - [Usage](#usage) 34 - [Development](#development) 35 - [Testing](#testing) 36 - [Deployment](#deployment) 37 - [License](#license) 38 39 ## Overview 40 41 Papai (**P**ersonal **A**droit **P**roactive **AI**) is a chat bot that enables natural language task management through any OpenAI-compatible LLM. Deploy it on Telegram, Mattermost, Discord, or Kontur Talk, connect it to Kaneo or YouTrack, and manage work through conversational task operations. Platform and task-provider instances are stored in SQLite after first bootstrap, so one deployment can manage multiple configured chat and task-provider instances. 42 43 The bot interprets natural-language requests, invokes capability-gated tools through LLM tool-calling, and replies with task details, updates, summaries, and search results. Personal and group settings are managed in the settings web UI launched via `/config` (requires `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`). Conversation history, memory, and memo storage are isolated by storage context. Telegram forum topics and Mattermost threads get separate thread-scoped context; Discord currently does not. 44 45 --- 46 47 ## Features 48 49 | Category | Capability | Description | 50 | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | 51 | **Tasks** | Create, Update, Search, List, Get, Delete | Full task lifecycle through natural language | 52 | **Comments** | Add, Read, Update, Delete, Reactions | Task discussions with provider-specific reactions | 53 | **Relations** | Blocks, Duplicates, Related, Subtask | Cross-task dependencies and associations | 54 | **Projects** | List, Create, Update, Delete, Team | Workspace organization and team management | 55 | **Statuses** | CRUD, Reorder | Board/status column management | 56 | **Labels** | List, Create, Update, Delete, Assign | Categorization and filtering | 57 | **Attachments** | List, Upload, Remove | Attach task files directly from chat messages where supported | 58 | **Collaboration** | Watchers, Votes, Visibility | Provider-dependent coordination surfaces | 59 | **Work Tracking** | Count tasks, log work, update work, remove work | Task counts and time tracking where supported | 60 | **Identity** | Link chat identity to tracker identity | Enables reliable “assign to me” and similar flows in groups | 61 | **History** | Thread-aware chat history lookup | Search the main group chat from a thread when more context is needed | 62 | **Web Fetch** | Public URL fetch, summary, excerpt | Fetch and summarize public web pages and PDFs | 63 | **Memory** | Conversation history, summary, facts | Context-aware multi-turn interactions | 64 | **Memos** | Save, search, list, promote | Quick notes with keyword or semantic lookup | 65 | **Recurring Tasks** | Template schedules | Reusable recurring task automation | 66 | **Deferred Prompts** | One-shot, delayed, cron | Scheduled proactive assistance | 67 | **Instructions** | Context-specific guidance | Per-chat custom instructions | 68 | **AI Output** | Show tool calls / reasoning; live status; sanitized or raw | Per-context control of the execution detail the bot posts to chat | 69 | **Plugins** | Trusted local extensions | Discover, approve, and enable first-party plugins per context | 70 | **MCP Servers** | External tools via Model Context Protocol | Merge tools from per-context or plugin-declared MCP servers | 71 72 ### Platform Support 73 74 | Platform | Group Message Model | Threads | Command Menu | Buttons | File messages directly | Message-scoped threads supported | No | No | No | No | JWT-authenticated; reply-context aware; minimal interaction surface | 80 81 ### Task Provider Support 82 83 | Provider | Auto-Provisioning | Relations | Statuses | Labels | Comments | Reactions | Team | Watchers / Votes / Visibility | Attachments | Work Items | Count | 84 | ------------ | ----------------- | --------- | -------- | ------ | -------- | --------- | ---- | ----------------------------- | ----------- | ---------- | ----- | 85 | **Kaneo** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | No | No | No | No | No | 86 | **YouTrack** | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | 87 88 YouTrack task creation can require workflow-specific custom fields. Papai exposes a `customFields` input on task creation for those project-specific requirements. 89 90 --- 91 92 ## Quick Start 93 94 ### Prerequisites 95 96 - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.3+ 97 - One supported chat platform: Telegram, Mattermost, Discord, or Kontur Talk 98 - One supported task provider: Kaneo or YouTrack 99 - OpenAI-compatible API credentials for your chosen model provider 100 101 ### 30-Second Setup 102 103 ```bash 104 git clone https://github.com/yourpapai/papai.git 105 cd papai 106 bun install 107 cp .env.example .env 108 ``` 109 110 Edit `.env`: 111 112 ```bash 113 # Required for all setups 114 ADMIN_USER_ID=123456789 # Your platform user ID 115 116 # First-run platform-instance bootstrap. Used only when the platform instance table is empty. 117 CHAT_PROVIDER=telegram # or: mattermost, discord, kontur-talk 118 # INSTANCE_CONFIG_KEY=64_hex_chars_for_production_config_encryption 119 120 # Central LLM credentials (seeded once into the provider registry on first start) 121 LLM_API_KEY=sk-... 122 LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 123 MAIN_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini 124 # SMALL_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini # optional, falls back to MAIN_MODEL 125 # EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small # optional, disables memo semantic search if unset 126 127 # Platform-specific 128 TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=your_token_here 129 ``` 130 131 > Task providers are no longer env-bootstrapped. After the bot starts, create a task 132 > instance via `/admin#instances`, then approve its plugin (`task-provider-kaneo` or 133 > `task-provider-youtrack`) in the settings web UI admin area (Plugins approval, super admin). The provider base URL is an 134 > instance config field set in `/admin#instances`, not an env var. 135 136 Start the bot: 137 138 ```bash 139 bun start 140 ``` 141 142 Then configure runtime settings: 143 144 1. Ensure `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is set to the bot's public base URL (e.g. `https://bot.example.com`) 145 2. DM the bot and run `/config` to receive a single-use link to the settings web UI 146 3. In the web UI Task provider section, bind the context to an active task instance, then enter its credentials (the credential fields appear only after a task instance is bound) and set your timezone 147 4. For group settings, open `/config` in DM and select the group context in the web UI 148 149 > LLM credentials are admin-owned and live in the `llm_providers` + `llm_admin_roles` SQLite tables. They are seeded from env vars on the first start that finds no provider configured, and can be managed later via the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections without restarting the bot. 150 151 > `CHAT_PROVIDER` seeds the first platform instance only when the platform instance table is empty. Task instances are never env-bootstrapped — create them via `/admin#instances` and approve the relevant task-provider plugin. After bootstrap, platform instances, task instances, and admins are managed from SQLite and the admin Instances surface (`/admin#instances`). 152 153 --- 154 155 ## Architecture 156 157 ```mermaid 158 flowchart TD 159 Runtime[src/index.ts] --> Router[ChatRouter] 160 Runtime --> Debug[Optional Debug Server + Debug/Admin UIs] 161 Router --> CP1[Telegram Instance] 162 Router --> CP2[Mattermost Instance] 163 Router --> CP3[Discord Instance] 164 Router --> CP4[Kontur Talk Instance] 165 User[User
Telegram / Mattermost / Discord / Kontur Talk] -->|Message or interaction| Router 166 Router -->|IncomingMessage / IncomingInteraction + platformInstanceId| Bot[bot.ts] 167 Bot -->|queued prompt + reply context + attachment ids| Queue[Message Queue + Attachment Workspace] 168 Queue --> LLM[LLM Orchestrator] 169 LLM --> Tools[Capability-gated Tool Registry] 170 Tools --> Providers[Task Providers] 171 Providers --> APIs[Task Tracker APIs] 172 Tools --> Web[Web Fetch / Extraction] 173 LLM --> Router 174 Router --> User 175 ``` 176 177 ### Component Overview 178 179 | Path | Responsibility | 180 | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 181 | `src/index.ts` | Entry point, env validation, startup, scheduler and optional debug server wiring | 182 | `src/bot.ts` | Bot setup: message ingress + auth, interaction routing, command wiring entry | 183 | `src/bot-command-wiring.ts` | Command registration and the observed command wrapper (post-auth analytics facts, reply tracking) | 184 | `src/bot-message-handler.ts` | Authorized message handling, mid-run steering, queueing, and the queued-turn lifecycle | 185 | `src/chat/` | Telegram, Mattermost, Discord, and Kontur Talk adapters plus capability metadata and the `ChatRouter` | 186 | `src/llm-orchestrator.ts` | LLM tool-calling orchestration | 187 | `src/tools/` | Context-aware, capability-gated tool assembly | 188 | `src/providers/` | Shared normalized provider types/utilities; Kaneo and YouTrack ship as first-party plugins | 189 | `src/instances/` | DB-backed platform/task/admin stores, encrypted instance config, and env bootstrap | 190 | `src/identity/` | Chat-to-provider identity mapping and “me” resolution | 191 | `src/attachments/` | Durable attachment workspace: ingest, S3 blob store, metadata, manifest building, resolver | 192 | `src/message-queue/` | Message coalescing and orderly LLM dispatch | 193 | `src/group-settings/` | Admin group-context listing, scope filtering, and group observations for the settings web UI | 194 | `src/web/` | Safe fetch, extraction, distillation, caching, and rate limiting for `web_fetch` | 195 | `src/plugins/` | Trusted local plugin system: discovery, manifest validation, approval, lifecycle, KV | 196 | `src/mcp/` | External MCP server adapter: connection pooling, tool namespacing, user + plugin endpoints | 197 | `src/analytics/` | Privacy-gated analytics: fact contracts, normalizer/runtime, instrumentation, session/outcome/friction materialization, governed usage backfill/reconciliation, retention/expiry enforcement, authenticated subject export/withdraw/delete, key rekey workflow, curated Metabase snapshot publisher/consumer coordinator (`analytics/metabase/`), thresholded aggregate delivery outbox (suppression lattice, DNS-pinned egress worker), bounded lifecycle jobs registered on the shared scheduler with cutover-fence admission (`analytics/jobs/register.ts`) | 198 | `src/debug/`, `client/debug/`, and `client/admin/` | Optional local debug server plus split `/debug` and `/admin` UIs | 199 200 --- 201 202 ## Configuration 203 204 ### Environment Variables 205 206
207 Startup And Bootstrap Variables (click to expand) 208 209 | Variable | When required | Description | Example | 210 | -------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | 211 | `ADMIN_USER_ID` | Always | Initial authorized admin identity | Platform user ID string seen by the active adapter | 212 | `CHAT_PROVIDER` | First run with empty platform DB | Platform bootstrap source (task providers are not env-bootstrapped) | `telegram`, `mattermost`, `discord`, or `kontur-talk` | 213 | `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | For the settings web UI | External base URL used to build single-use `/config` settings links; `/config` errors without it (the settings cookie is marked `Secure` only on HTTPS requests) | `https://bot.example.com` | 214 | `INSTANCE_CONFIG_KEY` | Production deployments | AES-256-GCM encryption key for platform/task instance config; fallback is host-local when unset | 64 hex chars | 215 216
217 218
219 Central LLM Credentials 220 221 LLM credentials are admin-owned and live in the `llm_providers` + `llm_admin_roles` SQLite tables. On the first start that finds no provider configured, a default provider is created from the env vars below and bound to the `main` role (and `small`/`embedding` if their env vars are present). After seeding, the bot reads them from the database on every startup; management happens in the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections (no restart needed for changes made there). 222 223 | Variable | Required | Description | 224 | ----------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 225 | `LLM_API_KEY` | Yes | API key for the OpenAI-compatible provider | 226 | `LLM_BASE_URL` | Yes | OpenAI-compatible base URL | 227 | `MAIN_MODEL` | Yes | Main model used for orchestration | 228 | `SMALL_MODEL` | No | Smaller helper model; callsites fall back to `main_model` when unset | 229 | `EMBEDDING_MODEL` | No | Embedding model for semantic memo search; when unset memo search degrades to keyword-only | 230 231 If no admin role binding exists after startup, the bot logs a startup warning and replies "the bot is not fully configured" to incoming messages until an admin configures a provider in the settings web UI. 232 233
234 235
236 Telegram Configuration 237 238 | Variable | Description | 239 | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | 240 | `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather) | 241 242 To find your Telegram numeric user ID, message [@userinfobot](https://t.me/userinfobot) and copy the returned value into `ADMIN_USER_ID`. 243 244 For Mattermost and Discord, use the platform user ID string the bot receives, not a display name or `@username`. 245 246 Authorized users added later through the settings UI admin area can be entered as `@username`: if the platform cannot resolve it to an ID (the Telegram Bot API cannot look up user accounts by username), the bot stores a pending entry and authorizes the user automatically the first time they message it. 247 248
249 250
251 Mattermost Configuration 252 253 | Variable | Description | 254 | ---------------------- | ------------------- | 255 | `MATTERMOST_URL` | Mattermost base URL | 256 | `MATTERMOST_BOT_TOKEN` | Bot account token | 257 258
259 260
261 Discord Configuration 262 263 | Variable | Description | 264 | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | 265 | `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` | Bot token from the Discord developer portal | 266 267 Discord support uses gateway intents including `MessageContent`. Enable the **Message Content Intent** for the bot in the Discord developer portal if you expect the bot to read message content beyond explicit interaction payloads. Verified applications must also enable the privileged Message Content intent in the portal for non-empty content, attachments, embeds, and similar fields. 268 269
270 271
272 Kontur Talk Configuration 273 274 | Variable | Description | 275 | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | 276 | `KONTUR_TALK_JWT_TOKEN` | JWT used to authenticate the bot against Kontur Talk | 277 278 Kontur Talk observes group messages directly and supports message-scoped threads. Its interaction surface is minimal: no command menu, buttons, or file transfer — only reply-context-aware messaging. `ADMIN_USER_ID` must match the Kontur Talk platform user ID string the bot receives. 279 280
281 282
283 Kaneo Configuration 284 285 Papai no longer reads Kaneo URLs from the environment. The Kaneo client URL is now a task-instance 286 config field: create the task instance in `/admin#instances`, then approve `task-provider-kaneo` in the 287 settings web UI admin area (Plugins approval). 288 Per-user credentials (`plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:credential`, `plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:workspaceId`) 289 are set in the settings web UI, opened via `/config`. 290 291 Kaneo can auto-provision user accounts for the bot workflow. In self-hosted deployments, `docker-compose.yml` 292 still expects Kaneo-service variables such as `KANEO_CLIENT_URL` (consumed by the bundled Kaneo and Caddy 293 services, not papai), `KANEO_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, and `KANEO_AUTH_SECRET`. 294 295
296 297
298 YouTrack Configuration 299 300 Papai no longer reads `YOUTRACK_URL` from the environment. The YouTrack instance URL is a task-instance 301 config field: create the task instance in `/admin#instances`, then approve `task-provider-youtrack` in the 302 settings web UI admin area (Plugins approval). 303 Runtime setup still requires a per-user token (`plugin:task-provider-youtrack:provider:token`), set in the 304 settings web UI, opened via `/config`. 305 306
307 308
309 Optional Debug Server 310 311 | Variable | Description | 312 | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 313 | `DEBUG_SERVER` | Set to `true` to start the local debug server | 314 | `DEBUG_HOSTNAME` | Debug server bind host (default `127.0.0.1`) | 315 | `DEBUG_PORT` | Debug server bind port (default `9100`) | 316 | `DASHBOARD_BASE_URL` | Origin embedded in the sign-in link (falls back to `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, then `http://{DEBUG_HOSTNAME}:{DEBUG_PORT}`) | 317 | `DASHBOARD_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` | Session lifetime (default `28800`, i.e. 8h) | 318 | `DASHBOARD_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS` | Sign-in link lifetime (default `300`, i.e. 5 min) | 319 320 `DEBUG_TOKEN` is no longer used; if set it is ignored and the bot logs a one-shot startup warning. Dashboard auth is now chat-issued. 321 322 When the debug server is enabled, the local surfaces are split by audience: 323 324 - `/debug` — engineer/live observability surface 325 - `/admin` — operator/configuration and durable records surface 326 - `/dashboard` — compatibility redirect to `/debug` 327 328 Admin sections include: 329 330 - **Billing** at `/admin#billing` — per-subject LLM usage from `llm_usage_events` (24h / 7d / 30d / all windows) and drill-down by request. 331 - **Stats** at `/admin#stats` — bot-wide anonymous structural counts and per-subject sub-panel backed by `GET /stats/global` and `GET /stats/subject/:id`. Both routes return counts, byte sizes, timestamps, enum distributions, and keyed-hashed identifiers only - never message text, memo bodies, observation text, attachment filenames, usernames, or other free-form content. 332 - **Instances** at `/admin#instances` — platform instances, task instances, and admin assignments backed by `/api/platform-instances`, `/api/task-instances`, and `/api/admins`. Instance config values are masked on read and encrypted at rest. If a persisted instance row cannot be decrypted or decoded, list routes return readable rows plus an `unreadable` diagnostics array instead of failing the whole response. LLM providers and role bindings are managed in the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections. 333 334 The dashboard is gated by a chat-issued session cookie rather than a static token. DM `/dashboard` to the bot to receive a single-use sign-in link (valid 5 min). Opening the link renders a confirmation page; pressing **Sign in** there consumes the link and sets an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` session cookie (8h default). The two-step page (consume on `POST`, not `GET`) keeps messaging-platform link-preview crawlers from burning the single-use link before you open it. `ADMIN_USER_ID` must match the chat user who runs `/dashboard`, and for HTTPS the reverse proxy must forward `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`. Never expose the dashboard on a public interface without upstream access control (e.g. a reverse-proxy auth layer or IP allowlist). 335 336
337 338
339 File Attachments (S3-compatible Object Storage) 340 341 Required when the bot needs to receive, persist, or attach files to tasks. 342 343 | Variable | Required | Description | 344 | ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | 345 | `S3_BUCKET` | Yes | S3 bucket name where attachment objects are stored | 346 | `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | Yes | Access key for the S3-compatible service | 347 | `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Yes | Secret key for the S3-compatible service | 348 | `S3_ENDPOINT` | No\* | Endpoint URL. Required for non-AWS providers such as MinIO, R2, or B2 | 349 | `S3_REGION` | No | AWS region (e.g. `us-east-1`) | 350 | `S3_PREFIX` | No | Optional key prefix inside the bucket | 351 | `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE` | No | Set to `true` for MinIO | 352 353
354 355
356 Analytics (Privacy-Gated, Off By Default) 357 358 papai ships a four-lane, privacy-gated analytics pipeline (`src/analytics/`). The shipping default is `local_aggregate` (closed daily counters only — no actor continuity); pseudonymous lanes require complete governance fields, both HMAC keyrings, and an explicit rollout stage. Operators: 359 360 | Variable | When required | Description | 361 | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 362 | `ANALYTICS_KILL_SWITCH` | Stage A; incident response | `1`/`true`/`on` forces every analytics lane off regardless of stored policy | 363 | `ANALYTICS_HMAC_KEYRING` | Pseudonymous longitudinal lane | Pseudonym keyring, `v1:<64-hex>[;v2:<64-hex>...]` | 364 | `ANALYTICS_GOVERNANCE_HMAC_KEYRING` | Pseudonymous longitudinal lane | Separate keyring for eligibility refs, consent fences, and deletion-bundle encryption | 365 | `ANALYTICS_SNAPSHOT_DIR` | Rekey BI coordination | Absolute dir holding published Metabase snapshot files; fail-closed without it | 366 | `ANALYTICS_BACKFILL_APPROVED_AT_MS` | Backfill under `legitimate_interest` | Operator approval timestamp used as the backfill policy cutoff | 367 368 Full operator flows, rollout stages A–E, and incident response: [`docs/operations/analytics-runbook.md`](docs/operations/analytics-runbook.md) and [`docs/operations/analytics-incident-runbook.md`](docs/operations/analytics-incident-runbook.md). 369 370
371 372 ### Runtime Configuration 373 374 Use the settings web UI to configure the bot. Launch it via `/config` in DM: 375 376 | Command | Description | 377 | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 378 | `/config` | Issues a single-use link to the settings web UI (requires `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` to be set) | 379 | `/clear` | Clear conversation history, summary, and facts for the current context | 380 | `/context` | View the current LLM context window for this conversation | 381 | `/dashboard` | DM, bot-admin only: receive a sign-in link to the operator debug/admin UI | 382 383 Settings managed in the web UI include: 384 385 | Key | Description | 386 | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | 387 | `plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:credential` | Kaneo API key or session token (plugin-namespaced) | 388 | `plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:workspaceId` | Kaneo workspace ID (plugin-namespaced) | 389 | `plugin:task-provider-youtrack:provider:token` | YouTrack permanent token (plugin-namespaced) | 390 | `timezone` | User timezone for local date/time interpretation | 391 | `mcp_endpoints` | JSON array of external MCP server endpoints whose tools are merged into the context (HTTPS only) | 392 393 LLM providers and role bindings are admin-owned and managed via env vars (first-start seed) or the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections - not through the user settings web UI. 394 395 Platform and task-provider base configuration is instance-owned. First-run env bootstrap creates a single `-default` platform instance row from `CHAT_PROVIDER` and the platform-specific env vars only when the platform instance table is empty. Task instances are never env-bootstrapped: create them through `/admin#instances` (or the admin section of the settings web UI) and approve the matching task-provider plugin. After that, manage instance lifecycle and admin assignment through `/admin#instances`; per-context credentials and preferences are managed in the settings web UI (reached via `/config`). 396 397 --- 398 399 ## Usage 400 401 Send natural-language requests to the bot. 402 403 **Task Management** 404 405 - "Create a high-priority bug: login crashes on Safari" 406 - "Move task 42 to In Progress" 407 - "Show me task PROJ-55" 408 - "Delete task 42" 409 410 **Comments and Relations** 411 412 - "Add a comment to task 42: waiting for API changes" 413 - "Show all comments on task 55" 414 - "Create a blocks relation: task 42 blocks task 55" 415 416 **Identity and Assignment** 417 418 - "I'm jsmith" 419 - "Assign this to me" 420 - "Add me as a watcher" 421 422 **Attachments and Web Fetch** 423 424 - Send a file with: "Attach this screenshot to task 42" 425 - "Fetch https://example.com/release-notes and summarize the breaking changes" 426 427 **Memos and History** 428 429 - "Save a memo: renew the SSL certificate before Friday" 430 - "Search my memos for certificate" 431 - "Look up what we decided about alert thresholds in the main chat" 432 433 ### Group Chat 434 435 Add the bot to a Telegram group, Mattermost channel, Discord server/channel, or Kontur Talk room. 436 437 Typical flow: 438 439 1. Add the bot to the group or channel 440 2. A group admin opens the settings web UI via `/config` in DM and authorizes members and configures group settings there 441 3. Members interact in-group, usually by mention where the platform requires it 442 443 Important behavior: 444 445 - Telegram and Mattermost can observe regular group messages; Discord group use is mention-driven. On Telegram and Discord, a user's reply to one of the bot's own messages in a group is treated like an `@mention` and processed without an explicit mention. 446 - Group configuration is done in the settings web UI (launched via `/config` in DM). 447 - Thread contexts are isolated. In Telegram forum topics and Mattermost threads, the bot stores thread-scoped history separately from the main group chat. 448 - In thread-scoped group contexts, the bot can use `lookup_group_history` to search the main group discussion when needed. 449 450 --- 451 452 ## Plugins 453 454 Papai supports trusted, repository-local first-party plugins that can contribute LLM tools, prompt fragments, bot commands, and scheduled jobs. The MVP is intentionally narrow: no sandbox, no marketplace, no npm install, no hot reload, no plugin secret store, and no raw chat/task/DB/env access. 455 456 ### Layout 457 458 ```text 459 plugins/ 460 └── / 461 ├── plugin.json # Zod-validated manifest 462 └── index.ts # default-exports a factory: () => ({ activate(ctx), deactivate?(ctx) }) 463 ``` 464 465 ### Lifecycle 466 467 1. **Discover** — startup scans `plugins/` and records each package in `plugin_admin_state` as `discovered`. The manifest + entry source are hashed for integrity. If the `plugins/` directory is missing and `DEBUG_SERVER=true`, startup fails fast (the settings web UI cannot dispatch task-provider provisioning without plugins); otherwise a `WARN` is logged and the bot starts in degraded mode. 468 2. **Approve** — bot admin approves the plugin in the settings web UI admin area. Any subsequent change to the manifest or entry source clears approval and requires re-approval. 469 3. **Activate** — on the next startup, approved plugins are imported with a per-plugin activation timeout. Failures are isolated and recorded to `plugin_runtime_events`. 470 4. **Enable per context** — once active, a plugin must be enabled for a personal or managed-group context via the settings web UI admin area or `defaultEnabled: true` in the manifest. 471 472 ### Contribution Surface 473 474 | Surface | Exposed as | Notes | 475 | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 476 | LLM tools | `plugin___` | Sandwiched through the same execution wrapper as core tools. | 477 | Prompt fragments | Appended to system prompt (8,000-char budget) | Synchronous only; 2,000 chars per fragment. | 478 | Commands | `plugin__` | Registered through the normal chat command path. | 479 | Scheduled jobs | Owner `plugin::` | Runs only for contexts where the plugin is enabled & eligible. | 480 | External MCP server | `plugin___` | Optional manifest `mcp` block; tools fetched from a Model Context Protocol server. | 481 482 ### Context API 483 484 Plugins activate against a frozen `PluginContext` exposing a scoped pino logger, a permission-gated KV store (`storage` permission required), and a `registration` facade. Tool executions also receive a `PluginToolRuntimeContext` with a permission-gated task-provider facade (`tasks.read` / `tasks.write` for read/write methods on `getTask`, `listTasks`, `searchTasks`, `createTask`, `updateTask`). Plugins never see raw chat or task providers, the DB, `process.env`, or arbitrary network access. 485 486 See [`docs/plugins/developer-guide.md`](docs/plugins/developer-guide.md) for the full manifest schema, factory contract, and permission semantics, plus the runnable example at [`docs/plugins/examples/hello-world/`](docs/plugins/examples/hello-world/). 487 488 ### Built-in Plugins 489 490 Papai ships with four first-party plugins under [`plugins/`](plugins/). All are `defaultEnabled: false` — approve each in the settings UI admin Plugins area (super admin) and enable it per context. Each plugin has its own README with manifest details, configuration, and behavior notes. 491 492 | Plugin | ID | Purpose | Permissions | 493 | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | 494 | [Audio Transcribe](plugins/audio-transcribe/README.md) | `audio-transcribe` | Auto-transcribes voice notes before the LLM turn and audio files on demand via an OpenAI-compatible API | `http`, `attachments.read`, `storage` | 495 | [Synthetic Web Search](plugins/synthetic-web-search/README.md) | `synthetic-web-search` | Web search via the Synthetic Search API; returns title/url/markdown text | `http` | 496 | [Kaneo](plugins/task-provider-kaneo/README.md) | `task-provider-kaneo` | Kaneo task-tracker integration (contributes the `kaneo` provider type; supports auto-provisioning) | `provider.task`, `identity`, `http` | 497 | [YouTrack](plugins/task-provider-youtrack/README.md) | `task-provider-youtrack` | YouTrack task-tracker integration (contributes the `youtrack` provider type; most fully-featured provider) | `provider.task`, `identity` | 498 499 --- 500 501 ## Development 502 503 All commands can be run as `bun

# PAPAI — Personal Adroit Proactive AI

Natural language task management for Telegram, Mattermost, Discord, and Kontur Talk

Quick Start · Features · Architecture · Configuration · Deployment

--- ## Table of Contents - [Overview](#overview) - [Features](#features) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Architecture](#architecture) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Usage](#usage) - [Development](#development) - [Testing](#testing) - [Deployment](#deployment) - [License](#license) ## Overview Papai (**P**ersonal **A**droit **P**roactive **AI**) is a chat bot that enables natural language task management through any OpenAI-compatible LLM. Deploy it on Telegram, Mattermost, Discord, or Kontur Talk, connect it to Kaneo or YouTrack, and manage work through conversational task operations. Platform and task-provider instances are stored in SQLite after first bootstrap, so one deployment can manage multiple configured chat and task-provider instances. The bot interprets natural-language requests, invokes capability-gated tools through LLM tool-calling, and replies with task details, updates, summaries, and search results. Personal and group settings are managed in the settings web UI launched via `/config` (requires `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`). Conversation history, memory, and memo storage are isolated by storage context. Telegram forum topics and Mattermost threads get separate thread-scoped context; Discord currently does not. --- ## Features | Category | Capability | Description | | -------------------- | Papai exposes a `customFields` input on task creation for those project-specific requirements. --- ## Quick Start ### Prerequisites - [Bun](https://bun.sh) 1.3+ - One supported chat platform: Telegram, Mattermost, Discord, or Kontur Talk - One supported task provider: Kaneo or YouTrack - OpenAI-compatible API credentials for your chosen model provider ### 30-Second Setup ```bash git clone https://github.com/yourpapai/papai.git cd papai bun install cp .env.example .env ``` Edit `.env`: ```bash # Required for all setups ADMIN_USER_ID=123456789 # Your platform user ID # First-run platform-instance bootstrap. Used only when the platform instance table is empty. CHAT_PROVIDER=telegram # or: mattermost, discord, kontur-talk # INSTANCE_CONFIG_KEY=64_hex_chars_for_production_config_encryption # Central LLM credentials (seeded once into the provider registry on first start) LLM_API_KEY=sk-... LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1 MAIN_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini # SMALL_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini # optional, falls back to MAIN_MODEL # EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small # optional, disables memo semantic search if unset # Platform-specific TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=your_token_here ``` > Task providers are no longer env-bootstrapped. After the bot starts, create a task > instance via `/admin#instances`, then approve its plugin (`task-provider-kaneo` or > `task-provider-youtrack`) in the settings web UI admin area (Plugins approval, super admin). The provider base URL is an > instance config field set in `/admin#instances`, not an env var. Start the bot: ```bash bun start ``` Then configure runtime settings: 1. Ensure `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is set to the bot's public base URL (e.g. `https://bot.example.com`) 2. DM the bot and run `/config` to receive a single-use link to the settings web UI 3. In the web UI Task provider section, bind the context to an active task instance, then enter its credentials (the credential fields appear only after a task instance is bound) and set your timezone 4. For group settings, open `/config` in DM and select the group context in the web UI > LLM credentials are admin-owned and live in the `llm_providers` + `llm_admin_roles` SQLite tables. They are seeded from env vars on the first start that finds no provider configured, and can be managed later via the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections without restarting the bot. > `CHAT_PROVIDER` seeds the first platform instance only when the platform instance table is empty. Task instances are never env-bootstrapped — create them via `/admin#instances` and approve the relevant task-provider plugin. After bootstrap, platform instances, task instances, and admins are managed from SQLite and the admin Instances surface (`/admin#instances`). --- ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD Runtime[src/index.ts] --> Router[ChatRouter] Runtime --> Debug[Optional Debug Server + Debug/Admin UIs] Router --> CP1[Telegram Instance] Router --> CP2[Mattermost Instance] Router --> CP3[Discord Instance] Router --> CP4[Kontur Talk Instance] User[User

Startup And Bootstrap Variables (click to expand) | Variable | When required | Description | Example | | -------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | | `ADMIN_USER_ID` | Always | Initial authorized admin identity | Platform user ID string seen by the active adapter | | `CHAT_PROVIDER` | First run with empty platform DB | Platform bootstrap source (task providers are not env-bootstrapped) | `telegram`, `mattermost`, `discord`, or `kontur-talk` | | `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` | For the settings web UI | External base URL used to build single-use `/config` settings links; `/config` errors without it (the settings cookie is marked `Secure` only on HTTPS requests) | `https://bot.example.com` | | `INSTANCE_CONFIG_KEY` | Production deployments | AES-256-GCM encryption key for platform/task instance config; fallback is host-local when unset | 64 hex chars |
Central LLM Credentials LLM credentials are admin-owned and live in the `llm_providers` + `llm_admin_roles` SQLite tables. On the first start that finds no provider configured, a default provider is created from the env vars below and bound to the `main` role (and `small`/`embedding` if their env vars are present). After seeding, the bot reads them from the database on every startup; management happens in the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections (no restart needed for changes made there). | Variable | Required | Description | | ----------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `LLM_API_KEY` | Yes | API key for the OpenAI-compatible provider | | `LLM_BASE_URL` | Yes | OpenAI-compatible base URL | | `MAIN_MODEL` | Yes | Main model used for orchestration | | `SMALL_MODEL` | No | Smaller helper model; callsites fall back to `main_model` when unset | | `EMBEDDING_MODEL` | No | Embedding model for semantic memo search; when unset memo search degrades to keyword-only | If no admin role binding exists after startup, the bot logs a startup warning and replies "the bot is not fully configured" to incoming messages until an admin configures a provider in the settings web UI.

Kaneo Configuration Papai no longer reads Kaneo URLs from the environment. The Kaneo client URL is now a task-instance config field: create the task instance in `/admin#instances`, then approve `task-provider-kaneo` in the settings web UI admin area (Plugins approval). Per-user credentials (`plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:credential`, `plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:workspaceId`) are set in the settings web UI, opened via `/config`. Kaneo can auto-provision user accounts for the bot workflow. In self-hosted deployments, `docker-compose.yml` still expects Kaneo-service variables such as `KANEO_CLIENT_URL` (consumed by the bundled Kaneo and Caddy services, not papai), `KANEO_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, and `KANEO_AUTH_SECRET`.
YouTrack Configuration Papai no longer reads `YOUTRACK_URL` from the environment. The YouTrack instance URL is a task-instance config field: create the task instance in `/admin#instances`, then approve `task-provider-youtrack` in the settings web UI admin area (Plugins approval). Runtime setup still requires a per-user token (`plugin:task-provider-youtrack:provider:token`), set in the settings web UI, opened via `/config`.
Optional Debug Server | Variable | Description | | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `DEBUG_SERVER` | Set to `true` to start the local debug server | | `DEBUG_HOSTNAME` | Debug server bind host (default `127.0.0.1`) | | `DEBUG_PORT` | Debug server bind port (default `9100`) | | `DASHBOARD_BASE_URL` | Origin embedded in the sign-in link (falls back to `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, then `http://{DEBUG_HOSTNAME}:{DEBUG_PORT}`) | | `DASHBOARD_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS` | Session lifetime (default `28800`, i.e. 8h) | | `DASHBOARD_CLAIM_TTL_SECONDS` | Sign-in link lifetime (default `300`, i.e. 5 min) | `DEBUG_TOKEN` is no longer used; if set it is ignored and the bot logs a one-shot startup warning. Dashboard auth is now chat-issued. When the debug server is enabled, the local surfaces are split by audience: - `/debug` — engineer/live observability surface - `/admin` — operator/configuration and durable records surface - `/dashboard` — compatibility redirect to `/debug` Admin sections include: - **Billing** at `/admin#billing` — per-subject LLM usage from `llm_usage_events` (24h / 7d / 30d / all windows) and drill-down by request. - **Stats** at `/admin#stats` — bot-wide anonymous structural counts and per-subject sub-panel backed by `GET /stats/global` and `GET /stats/subject/:id`. Both routes return counts, byte sizes, timestamps, enum distributions, and keyed-hashed identifiers only - never message text, memo bodies, observation text, attachment filenames, usernames, or other free-form content. - **Instances** at `/admin#instances` — platform instances, task instances, and admin assignments backed by `/api/platform-instances`, `/api/task-instances`, and `/api/admins`. Instance config values are masked on read and encrypted at rest. If a persisted instance row cannot be decrypted or decoded, list routes return readable rows plus an `unreadable` diagnostics array instead of failing the whole response. LLM providers and role bindings are managed in the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections. The dashboard is gated by a chat-issued session cookie rather than a static token. DM `/dashboard` to the bot to receive a single-use sign-in link (valid 5 min). Opening the link renders a confirmation page; pressing **Sign in** there consumes the link and sets an `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` session cookie (8h default). The two-step page (consume on `POST`, not `GET`) keeps messaging-platform link-preview crawlers from burning the single-use link before you open it. `ADMIN_USER_ID` must match the chat user who runs `/dashboard`, and for HTTPS the reverse proxy must forward `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`. Never expose the dashboard on a public interface without upstream access control (e.g. a reverse-proxy auth layer or IP allowlist).

The shipping default is `local_aggregate` (closed daily counters only — no actor continuity); pseudonymous lanes require complete governance fields, both HMAC keyrings, and an explicit rollout stage. Operators: | Variable | When required | Description | | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `ANALYTICS_KILL_SWITCH` | Stage A; incident response | `1`/`true`/`on` forces every analytics lane off regardless of stored policy | | `ANALYTICS_HMAC_KEYRING` | Pseudonymous longitudinal lane | Pseudonym keyring, `v1:<64-hex>[;v2:<64-hex>...]` | | `ANALYTICS_GOVERNANCE_HMAC_KEYRING` | Pseudonymous longitudinal lane | Separate keyring for eligibility refs, consent fences, and deletion-bundle encryption | | `ANALYTICS_SNAPSHOT_DIR` | Rekey BI coordination | Absolute dir holding published Metabase snapshot files; fail-closed without it | | `ANALYTICS_BACKFILL_APPROVED_AT_MS` | Backfill under `legitimate_interest` | Operator approval timestamp used as the backfill policy cutoff | Full operator flows, rollout stages A–E, and incident response: [`docs/operations/analytics-runbook.md`](docs/operations/analytics-runbook.md) and [`docs/operations/analytics-incident-runbook.md`](docs/operations/analytics-incident-runbook.md).
### Runtime Configuration Use the settings web UI to configure the bot. Launch it via `/config` in DM: | Command | Description | | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/config` | Issues a single-use link to the settings web UI (requires `SETTINGS_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` to be set) | | `/clear` | Clear conversation history, summary, and facts for the current context | | `/context` | View the current LLM context window for this conversation | | `/dashboard` | DM, bot-admin only: receive a sign-in link to the operator debug/admin UI | Settings managed in the web UI include: | Key | Description | | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:credential` | Kaneo API key or session token (plugin-namespaced) | | `plugin:task-provider-kaneo:provider:workspaceId` | Kaneo workspace ID (plugin-namespaced) | | `plugin:task-provider-youtrack:provider:token` | YouTrack permanent token (plugin-namespaced) | | `timezone` | User timezone for local date/time interpretation | | `mcp_endpoints` | JSON array of external MCP server endpoints whose tools are merged into the context (HTTPS only) | LLM providers and role bindings are admin-owned and managed via env vars (first-start seed) or the settings admin Providers + LLM Roles sections - not through the user settings web UI. Platform and task-provider base configuration is instance-owned. First-run env bootstrap creates a single `-default` platform instance row from `CHAT_PROVIDER` and the platform-specific env vars only when the platform instance table is empty. Task instances are never env-bootstrapped: create them through `/admin#instances` (or the admin section of the settings web UI) and approve the matching task-provider plugin. After that, manage instance lifecycle and admin assignment through `/admin#instances`; per-context credentials and preferences are managed in the settings web UI (reached via `/config`). --- ## Usage Send natural-language requests to the bot. **Task Management** - "Create a high-priority bug: login crashes on Safari" - "Move task 42 to In Progress" - "Show me task PROJ-55" - "Delete task 42" **Comments and Relations** - "Add a comment to task 42: waiting for API changes" - "Show all comments on task 55" - "Create a blocks relation: task 42 blocks task 55" **Identity and Assignment** - "I'm jsmith" - "Assign this to me" - "Add me as a watcher" **Attachments and Web Fetch** - Send a file with: "Attach this screenshot to task 42" - "Fetch https://example.com/release-notes and summarize the breaking changes" **Memos and History** - "Save a memo: renew the SSL certificate before Friday" - "Search my memos for certificate" - "Look up what we decided about alert thresholds in the main chat" ### Group Chat Add the bot to a Telegram group, Mattermost channel, Discord server/channel, or Kontur Talk room. Typical flow: 1. Add the bot to the group or channel 2. A group admin opens the settings web UI via `/config` in DM and authorizes members and configures group settings there 3. Members interact in-group, usually by mention where the platform requires it Important behavior: - Telegram and Mattermost can observe regular group messages; Discord group use is mention-driven. On Telegram and Discord, a user's reply to one of the bot's own messages in a group is treated like an `@mention` and processed without an explicit mention. - Group configuration is done in the settings web UI (launched via `/config` in DM). - Thread contexts are isolated. In Telegram forum topics and Mattermost threads, the bot stores thread-scoped history separately from the main group chat. - In thread-scoped group contexts, the bot can use `lookup_group_history` to search the main group discussion when needed. --- ## Plugins Papai supports trusted, repository-local first-party plugins that can contribute LLM tools, prompt fragments, bot commands, and scheduled jobs. The MVP is intentionally narrow: no sandbox, no marketplace, no npm install, no hot reload, no plugin secret store, and no raw chat/task/DB/env access. ### Layout ```text plugins/ └── / ├── plugin.json # Zod-validated manifest └── index.ts # default-exports a factory: () => ({ activate(ctx), deactivate?(ctx) }) ``` ### Lifecycle 1. **Discover** — startup scans `plugins/` and records each package in `plugin_admin_state` as `discovered`. The manifest + entry source are hashed for integrity. If the `plugins/` directory is missing and `DEBUG_SERVER=true`, startup fails fast (the settings web UI cannot dispatch task-provider provisioning without plugins); otherwise a `WARN` is logged and the bot starts in degraded mode. 2. **Approve** — bot admin approves the plugin in the settings web UI admin area. Any subsequent change to the manifest or entry source clears approval and requires re-approval. 3. **Activate** — on the next startup, approved plugins are imported with a per-plugin activation timeout. Failures are isolated and recorded to `plugin_runtime_events`. 4. **Enable per context** — once active, a plugin must be enabled for a personal or managed-group context via the settings web UI admin area or `defaultEnabled: true` in the manifest. ### Contribution Surface | Surface | Exposed as | Notes | | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | LLM tools | `plugin___` | Sandwiched through the same execution wrapper as core tools. | | Prompt fragments | Appended to system prompt (8,000-char budget) | Synchronous only; 2,000 chars per fragment. | | Commands | `plugin__` | Registered through the normal chat command path. | | Scheduled jobs | Owner `plugin::` | Runs only for contexts where the plugin is enabled & eligible. | | External MCP server | `plugin___` | Optional manifest `mcp` block; tools fetched from a Model Context Protocol server. | ### Context API Plugins activate against a frozen `PluginContext` exposing a scoped pino logger, a permission-gated KV store (`storage` permission required), and a `registration` facade. Tool executions also receive a `PluginToolRuntimeContext` with a permission-gated task-provider facade (`tasks.read` / `tasks.write` for read/write methods on `getTask`, `listTasks`, `searchTasks`, `createTask`, `updateTask`). Plugins never see raw chat or task providers, the DB, `process.env`, or arbitrary network access. See [`docs/plugins/developer-guide.md`](docs/plugins/developer-guide.md) for the full manifest schema, factory contract, and permission semantics, plus the runnable example at [`docs/plugins/examples/hello-world/`](docs/plugins/examples/hello-world/). ### Built-in Plugins Papai ships with four first-party plugins under [`plugins/`](plugins/). All are `defaultEnabled: false` — approve each in the settings UI admin Plugins area (super admin) and enable it per context. Each plugin has its own README with manifest details, configuration, and behavior notes. | Plugin | ID | Purpose | Permissions | | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | | [Audio Transcribe](plugins/audio-transcribe/README.md) | `audio-transcribe` | Auto-transcribes voice notes before the LLM turn and audio files on demand via an OpenAI-compatible API | `http`, `attachments.read`, `storage` | | [Synthetic Web Search](plugins/synthetic-web-search/README.md) | `synthetic-web-search` | Web search via the Synthetic Search API; returns title/url/markdown text | `http` | | [Kaneo](plugins/task-provider-kaneo/README.md) | `task-provider-kaneo` | Kaneo task-tracker integration (contributes the `kaneo` provider type; supports auto-provisioning) | `provider.task`, `identity`, `http` | | [YouTrack](plugins/task-provider-youtrack/README.md) | `task-provider-youtrack` | YouTrack task-tracker integration (contributes the `youtrack` provider type; most fully-featured provider) | `provider.task`, `identity` | --- ## Development All commands can be run as `bun
